text: A firstorder autoregressive AR time series Yt Yt t is said to be nearly nonstationary if is close to For a nearly nonstationary AR model it is shown that the limiting distribution of the least squares estimate of obtained by Chan and Wei can be expressed as a functional of the OrnsteinUhlenbeck process This alternative expression provides a simple and efficient means to tabulate the percentiles of the limiting distribution that furnishes a useful procedure to test for near nonstationarity Based on the eigenvalueeigenfunction consideration it is shown that the OrnsteinUhlenbeck formulation possesses an infinite series expansion that extends the result of Dickey and Fuller to the nearly nonstationary model Numerical calculations based on different representations of the limiting distribution are performed and compared It is found that the OrnsteinUhlenbeck expression provides a better algorithm for tabulating the percentiles Applications to other time series are also considered

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: ValueatRisk VaR is a commonly used risk measure adopted by financial engineers and regulators alike Many of the techniques used in calculating VaR however rely on simulations that can be difficult and time consuming One of the objectives of this paper is to conduct statistical inference for VaR based on saddle point approximation and volatility estimation Specifically by assuming that the loss distribution is a generalized hyperbolic we propose a quasiresidual based volatility estimate Because saddle point approximation furnishes a fast and accurate means to approximate the loss distribution and its percentiles including the VaR in particular it is then used to approximate the loss distribution of the quasiresiduals from which VaR can be estimated Simulation studies and data analysis confirm that the proposed methodology works well both in theory and practice

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: This paper studies the quasimaximum likelihood estimator QMLE of nonstationary GARCHp q models By expressing GARCH models in matrix form the loglikelihood function is written in terms of the product of random matrices Oseledecs multiplicative ergodic theorem is then used to establish the asymptotic properties of the loglikelihood function and thereby showing the weak consistency and the asymptotic normality of the QMLE for nonstationary GARCHp q models

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: This paper studies asymptotic properties of the exact maximum likelihood estimates MLE for a general class of Gaussian seasonal longrangedependent processes This class includes the commonly used Gegenbauer and seasonal autoregressive fractionally integrated moving average processes By means of an approximation of the spectral density the exact MLE of this class are shown to be consistent asymptotically normal and efficient Finite sample performance of these estimates is examined by Monte Carlo simulations and it is shown that the estimates behave very well even for moderate sample sizes The estimation methodology is illustrated by a reallife Internet traffic example

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for conducting likelihood inferences in highdimensional factor analysis of time series data with a particular focus on its applications in finance As financial markets increasingly exhibit complex interdependencies and high dimensionality traditional analytical approaches fall short of capturing the underlying factors driving asset movements We propose a novel estimation technique that leverages advanced statistical methods including penalized likelihood and Bayesian approaches to extract latent factors from highdimensional time series datasets Our framework allows for the estimation of factor loadings and noise variances while ensuring computational efficiency through the implementation of variational inference methods We validate our approach using simulated datasets and apply it to realworld financial time series revealing critical insights into market dynamics and the relationships between risk factors Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of highdimensional factor analysis in uncovering hidden structures within financial data providing a powerful tool for portfolio management and risk assessment The findings suggest that our methodology not only enhances the understanding of financial systems but also paves the way for future research in highdimensional statistical modeling in various fields

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: This article investigates likelihood inferences for highdimensional factor analysis of time series data We develop a matrix decomposition technique to obtain expressions of the likelihood functions and its derivatives With such expressions the traditional delta method that relies heavily on score function and Hessian matrix can be extended to highdimensional cases We establish asymptotic theories including consistency and asymptotic normality Moreover fast computational algorithms are developed for estimation Applications to highdimensional stock price data and portfolio analysis are discussed The technical proofs of the asymptotic results and the computer codes are available online

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this study we propose a comprehensive framework for making statistical inferences in nonstationary Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity GARCH models specifically the GARCHp Q class Nonstationarity in financial data characterized by timevarying mean and volatility poses significant challenges for traditional GARCH modeling approaches which assume stationarity We derive asymptotic distributions for the estimators of model parameters under nonstationary conditions and introduce a robust estimation procedure that accommodates trends and structural breaks Our methodology includes a novel application of quasimaximum likelihood estimation in conjunction with unit root tests to validate the nonstationarity of the conditional variance We also explore the implications of nonstationarity on model diagnostics and forecasting performance Extensive Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate the finite sample properties of our estimators showcasing their consistency and asymptotic normality Finally we apply our developed framework to several financial time series datasets to illustrate its practical utility and effectiveness in capturing dynamic volatility patterns The results emphasize the importance of accounting for nonstationarity in GARCH models for accurate risk assessment and better decisionmaking in finance

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this paper we investigate the properties and implications of nonstationary autoregressive processes with infinite variance expanding upon traditional models that assume finite variance We introduce a novel framework that captures the dynamics of nonstationary time series while acknowledging the complexities introduced by infinite variance Using a blend of theoretical derivations and empirical analysis we demonstrate how these processes can be characterized by their asymptotic behavior and longrange dependence properties We establish sufficient conditions for the existence of such processes and provide influential examples to illustrate their applications in fields such as finance and environmental science The consequences of modeling choices are examined revealing that failure to account for infinite variance can lead to significant underestimation of risks and misinterpretation of longterm forecasts Our findings suggest new methodologies for analyzing and forecasting nonstationary time series data paving the way for enhanced models that incorporate the intricacies of infinite variance dynamics Through simulation studies we evaluate the performance of our proposed estimators emphasizing their robustness in capturing the unpredictable nature of realworld phenomena Overall our work contributes to the existing literature by providing a comprehensive analysis of nonstationary autoregressive processes in the context of infinite variance offering critical insights for researchers and practitioners

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the Saddle Point Approximation SPA methodology as it applies to the estimation of ValueatRisk VaR under various market conditions VaR is a critical risk management tool in finance assessing the potential loss in value of an asset or portfolio over a specified time frame at a given confidence level Traditional methods of VaR estimation often rely on assumptions of normality or specific distributional forms which may not hold in realworld scenarios particularly in the presence of heavy tails and skewness By employing the SPA technique we derive more accurate approximations of the distribution of portfolio returns enabling a more robust estimation of VaR that accounts for the underlying volatility dynamics We compare the performance of the SPAbased VaR estimates against conventional approaches including historical simulation and parametric methods using both simulated data and historical market returns Our results demonstrate that the SPA method provides significant improvements in both accuracy and reliability particularly in periods of heightened market stress The implications for financial risk management and regulatory compliance are discussed emphasizing the need for adaptive approaches in the calculation of risk metrics This study contributes to the growing body of literature on advanced statistical techniques for risk assessment offering enhanced methodologies that can be integrated into risk management frameworks across financial institutions

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this paper we investigate parameter inference in nearly nonstationary time series a common phenomenon in empirical data where the underlying processes exhibit longterm trends or shifts that can complicate traditional statistical modeling We introduce a novel framework that integrates methodologies from both time series analysis and nonstationary process theory enabling robust estimation of parameters in the presence of subtle nonstationary behaviors Our approach employs a combination of statespace models and filtering techniques to disentangle the stationary and nonstationary components facilitating a clearer understanding of the underlying dynamics We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through a series of simulation studies and realworld applications highlighting its superior performance in parameter estimation accuracy when compared to conventional techniques Furthermore we discuss the implications of our findings for practitioners dealing with economic environmental and social data that display nearly nonstationary characteristics Our results contribute to the ongoing discourse on improving statistical inference in complex time series providing a comprehensive toolset for researchers and analysts in various fields

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this paper we explore quantile inference in the context of heteroscedastic regression models where the error variance is not constant across observations Traditional methods of regression analysis often rely on the assumption of homoscedasticity which can lead to biased estimates and incorrect inference when this assumption is violated We propose a novel framework for quantile regression that explicitly accommodates heteroscedasticity by modeling the conditional quantiles of the response variable using a flexible approach that incorporates varying error structures Our method leverages robust statistical techniques to provide consistent estimation and inference for quantile parameters We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through simulation studies and application to realworld data illustrating its advantages over conventional methods in terms of accuracy and reliability The findings offer valuable insights for practitioners seeking to understand the relationship between predictors and response variables in the presence of unequal variances thereby enhancing the robustness of quantilebased inferences in regression analysis

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In the realm of credit risk assessment understanding the dynamics of credit migration where borrowers transition between different credit risk categories is crucial for effective risk management and capital allocation This paper presents a comprehensive structural model of credit migration that integrates macroeconomic factors borrowerspecific characteristics and market conditions to predict changes in credit quality over time We employ a hybrid approach combining Markov chain processes and logistic regression to capture the probabilistic nature of migrations across credit ratings Our model is calibrated using a large dataset of historical credit ratings and associated economic indicators allowing us to identify key drivers of credit transitions We validate our model through outofsample testing demonstrating its superior predictive power compared to traditional models The findings provide a robust framework for financial institutions seeking to enhance their credit risk models facilitate stress testing and optimize portfolio management strategies Additionally we discuss the implications of credit migration dynamics on regulatory capital requirements and potential policy responses in changing economic landscapes

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: Credit migrations constitute the building blocks of modern risk management A firmspecific structural model of credit migration that incorporates the firms capital structure and the risk perception of rating agencies is proposed The proposed model employs the notion of distancetodefault which quantifies default probability The properties of Brownian excursions play an essential role in the analysis The proposed model not only allows the derivation of closedform credit transition probability but also provides plausible explanations for certain empirical evidence such as the default probability overlaps in ratings and the slowtorespond feature of rating agencies The proposed model is calibrated through simulations and applied to empirical data which show rating agencies risk perceptions to be significant The calibrated model allows calculation of the firmspecific transition probabilities of rated companies C Elsevier BV

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: Consider the nonparametric heteroscedastic regression model Y mX sigmaXepsilon where m is an unknown conditional mean function and sigma is an unknown conditional scale function In this paper the limit distribution of the quantile estimate for the scale function sigmaX is derived Since the limit distribution depends on the unknown density of the errors an empirical likelihood ratio statistic based on quantile estimator is proposed This statistics is used to construct confidence intervals for the variance function Under certain regularity conditions it is shown that the quantile estimate of the scale function converges to a Brownian motion and the empirical likelihood ratio statistic converges to a chisquared random variable Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over the least squares procedure when the underlying errors have heavy tails C Elsevier BV

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: Consider an ARp process where t is a sequence of iid random variables lying in the domain of attraction of a stable law with index a This time series is said to be a nonstationary ARp process if at least one of its characteristic roots lies on the unit circle The limit distribution of the least squares estimator LSE of for with infinite variance innovation t is established in this paper In particular by virtue of the result of Kurtz and Protter of stochastic integrals it is shown that the limit distribution of the LSE is a functional of integrated stable process Simulations for the estimator of beta and its limit distribution are also given

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this paper we investigate the efficient estimation of seasonal longrangedependent processes which are characterized by persistent autocorrelations that exhibit varying periodic structures Traditional approaches often struggle to accurately capture the complexities inherent in such data particularly when it comes to estimating longrange dependence accurately due to seasonal effects We propose a novel estimation framework that employs a combination of wavelet analysis and generalized method of moments GMM to enhance the estimation process Our methodology allows for the simultaneous modeling of both seasonal and longrange dependence characteristics thus providing a more robust treatment of complex time series data We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through extensive simulation studies and empirical applications to realworld datasets comparing our method to existing techniques in terms of bias variance and mean squared error Results indicate significant improvements in estimation efficiency and accuracy ultimately contributing to better forecasting and understanding of seasonal longrangedependent phenomena The implications of our findings for fields such as economics environmental science and finance are discussed highlighting the relevance of accurate estimates in policymaking and strategic planning

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: Random walk models driven by GARCH errors are widely applicable in diverse areas in finance and econometrics For a firstorder autoregressive model driven by GARCH errors let phi over cap n be the least squares estimate of the autoregressive coefficient The asymptotic distribution of phi over cap n is given in Ling and Li when the GARCH errors have finite variances In this paper the limit distribution of phi over cap n is established as functionals of a stable process when the GARCH errors are heavytailed with infinite variances An estimate of the tail index of the limiting stable process is proposed and its asymptotic properties are derived Furthermore it is shown that the least absolute deviations procedure works well under the unitroot and heavytailed GARCH setting This research provides a relatively broad treatment of unitroot GARCH models that includes the commonly entertained unitroot IGARCH scenario

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: This paper investigates the limit behavior of quadratic forms derived from longmemory linear processes with heavytailed GARCH Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity innovations We establish necessary conditions for convergence and identify the asymptotic distributions of these quadratic forms considering the intricate interplay between the longmemory properties of the underlying processes and the heavytailed nature of the GARCH innovations We utilize advanced techniques from the theory of stochastic processes and statistical inference to analyze the spectral properties and the dependence structure inherent in the quadratic forms Our findings reveal that under suitable regularity conditions the limiting distribution can be characterized by a stable law highlighting the impact of the heavytailed phenomenon in the context of longmemory processes Moreover we provide a series of simulation studies that validate the theoretical results and illustrate their practical implications in financial applications particularly in risk assessment and portfolio optimization This study contributes to the understanding of the asymptotic behavior of quadratic forms in complex stochastic settings paving the way for further research on robust statistical inference in the presence of longrange dependence and extreme value events

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: This paper investigates the inferential properties of unitroot models disturbed by errors characterized by infinite variance GARCH Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity processes Traditional approaches to unitroot testing often assume that the error terms have finite variance potentially leading to misleading conclusions when applied to time series data exhibiting heavytailed distributions By extending the classical unitroot frameworks to accommodate the infinite variance case we develop new testing procedures that maintain consistency and asymptotic normality even under these conditions Our analysis includes both theoretical derivations and empirical evaluations demonstrating that conventional tests can yield invalid results in the presence of GARCH errors with infinite variance We propose a robust framework for conducting inference utilizing generalized methods of moments GMM to estimate parameters and perform hypothesis testing Through Monte Carlo simulations we assess the size and power of our proposed tests compared to existing methodologies Finally we apply our findings to realworld financial time series data illustrating the practical implications of ignoring the potential for infinite variance in GARCH models The results highlight the importance of careful selection of testing procedures when analyzing unitroot processes in volatile environments

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: This paper explores the application of empirical likelihood methods to autoregressive models particularly focusing on their performance in handling unstable time series data We begin by outlining the theoretical foundation of empirical likelihood emphasizing its advantages over traditional likelihood approaches such as robustness to model misspecification and the ability to incorporate constraints without reliance on parametric forms We then extend the empirical likelihood framework to autoregressive models proposing new estimation techniques that can effectively capture the dynamic structures inherent in unstable time series Through simulation studies we illustrate the finitesample properties of our proposed estimators demonstrating their superior performance in bias and variance relative to conventional methods under various scenarios of instability Furthermore we present applications to realworld data exhibiting characteristics of instability such as economic indicators and environmental measurements highlighting the practical implications of our findings The results indicate that empirical likelihood methods can offer a viable alternative for modeling and inference in the presence of autoregressive patterns contributing to a deeper understanding of complex timedependent phenomena

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this paper we investigate the properties of longmemory time series with a focus on establishing moment bounds and the mean squared prediction errors MSPE Longmemory processes characterized by their persistent correlations over time present unique challenges in forecasting and inference We provide rigorous mathematical formulations to derive moment bounds that elucidate the behavior of time series with varying degrees of long memory Utilizing these bounds we conduct a comprehensive analysis of the MSPE under different model specifications highlighting the conditions under which optimal predictions can be achieved Empirical applications are presented to illustrate the practical implications of our theoretical findings including a case study on financial data exhibiting longrange dependence Our results not only contribute to the theoretical understanding of longmemory processes but also provide valuable insights for practitioners in time series forecasting emphasizing the importance of incorporating longterm dependencies into predictive models

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In the analysis of nonstationary time series traditional empirical processes often fall short in capturing the complexities introduced by timevarying distributions and trends This paper introduces a novel framework of marked empirical processes tailored specifically for nonstationary time series data By incorporating markers that reflect significant features of the time series such as trends seasonality and structural breaks our approach enhances the interpretability and robustness of empirical distributions over various temporal intervals We establish consistency and asymptotic properties of the proposed marked empirical processes and demonstrate their efficacy through simulations and realworld applications Our findings suggest that marked empirical processes provide an effective tool for modeling nonstationary phenomena offering improved insights into the underlying dynamics of complex temporal data This work contributes to the broader field of statistical methods for time series analysis by extending the utility of empirical processes in nonstationary contexts thereby facilitating better inference in diverse applications ranging from finance to environmental science

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: Empirical likelihood is developed for autoregressive models with innovations that form a martingale difference sequence Limiting distributions of the log empirical likelihood ratio statistic for both the stable and unstable cases axe established Behavior of the log empirical likelihood ratio statistic is considered in nearly nonstationary models to assess the local power of unit root tests and to construct confidence intervals Resampling methods are proposed to improve the finitesample performance of empirical likelihood statistics This paper shows that empirical likelihood methodology compares favorably with existing methods and demonstrates its potential for time series with more general innovation structures

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: Bandwidth selection has been an important topic in nonparametric density estimation In this paper an effective method for local bandwidth selection is proposed For local bandwidth selection due to data sparsity and other reasons extremely small bandwidths are sometimes selected which lead to severe undersmoothing To circumvent this difficulty the main idea behind the proposed method is to choose the largest bandwidth that still achieves the optimal rate When coupled with practical bias reduction techniques the bandwidth selected from this method can be applied simultaneously to conduct both local point and interval estimation Simulation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach which compares favorably with other existing approaches C Elsevier BV

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: AbstractIn this paper we explore nonparametric local inference techniques for density estimation focusing on their utility and robustness in handling complex data structures While traditional parametric methods often impose restrictive assumptions about the underlying distribution nonparametric approaches offer greater flexibility allowing for more accurate representation of the data We introduce a novel framework that integrates local inference methods such as kernel density estimation and local polynomial fitting with contemporary statistical tools like bootstrap resampling and crossvalidation Our results demonstrate that this combined approach not only enhances the reliability of density estimates but also improves the accuracy of confidence intervals and hypothesis testing in practical scenarios Through comprehensive simulations and realdata applications we illustrate the effectiveness of our proposed methodology providing insights into optimal bandwidth selection and the impact of local neighborhood size This work contributes to the growing field of nonparametric statistics by offering a robust alternative for density estimation that can be applied in various disciplines including finance biology and environmental science We conclude with discussions on future directions for research and application emphasizing the potential of nonparametric local inference as a critical tool in modern statistical analysis

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: A moment bound for the normalized conditionalsumofsquares CSS estimate of a general autoregressive fractionally integrated moving average ARFIMA model with an arbitrary unknown memory parameter is derived in this paper To achieve this goal a uniform moment bound for the inverse of the normalized objective function is established An important application of these results is to establish asymptotic expressions for the onestep and multistep mean squared prediction errors MSPE of the CSS predictor These asymptotic expressions not only explicitly demonstrate how the multistep MSPE of the CSS predictor manifests with the model complexity and the dependent structure but also offer means to compare the performance of the CSS predictor with the least squares LS predictor for integrated autoregressive models It turns out that the CSS predictor can gain substantial advantage over the LS predictor when the integration order is high Numerical findings are also conducted to illustrate the theoretical results

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this article accumulated sudden infant death syndrome SIDS data from and for the counties of North Carolina are analyzed After a spatial exploratory data analysis Markov randomfield models are fit to the data The spatial trend is meant to capture the largescale variation in the data and the variance and spatial dependence are meant to capture the smallscale variation The trend could be a function of other explanatory variables or could simply be modeled as a function of spatial location Both models are fit and compared The results give an excellent illustration of a phenomenon already wellknown in time series that autocorrelation in data can be due to an undiscovered explanatory variable Indeed for we confirm a dependence of SIDS rate on proportion of nonwhite babies born along with insignificant spatial correlation Without this regressor variable however the spatial correlation is significant In perhaps due to reporting bias or the effect of publiceducation programs in infant health the proportion of nonwhite babies born is no longer an important explanatory variable SIDS is currently a leading category of postneonatal death yet its cause is still a mystery It accounts for about deaths a year in the United States taking the lives of about two infants per live births In contrast to the usual pathologic and physiologic studies of SIDS this article takes an epidemiologic approach using data available at the county level The SIDS data analyzed are in a form that is representative of many problems encountered in the health and social sciences Counts of individuals from a known or estimated base occur in epidemiologic studies eg consider cancer incidence in a particular year from the base of population years at risk for US counties census surveys eg for assessing undercount consider the dualsystem estimate of uncounted people in a decennial census from the base of total number of people for US states and so forth It is hoped that the spatial methods presented will prove useful in a variety of such problems

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: This paper investigates the convergence properties of stochastic integrals through the lens of white noise calculus establishing a robust framework for analyzing convergence in stochastic processes We begin by reviewing the foundational principles of white noise analysis and its implications for stochastic calculus highlighting how these tools can enhance our understanding of integrals driven by Gaussian white noise Utilizing rigorous mathematical techniques we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the convergence of stochastic integrals in various settings including both finite and infinitedimensional spaces Furthermore we explore the relationships between different modes of convergence almost sure in probability and in distribution providing illustrative examples that underscore the practical applications of our findings Our results contribute to the theoretical underpinnings of stochastic analysis and offer new insights applicable to fields such as finance physics and engineering where the modeling of uncertainty is paramount We conclude with a discussion of potential extensions of our work suggesting avenues for future research in the realm of nonlinear stochastic systems

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this paper we investigate the properties of Mestimation in the context of nonparametric regression models characterized by strong dependence and infinite variance Traditional Mestimation methods often assume independent or weakly dependent data which limits their applicability in realworld scenarios where such conditions are violated We develop a robust theoretical framework to analyze the consistency and asymptotic normality of Mestimators under these challenging conditions Our approach leverages advanced techniques from both dependence theory and robust statistics to address the intricacies introduced by strong dependence and infinite variance We establish a set of sufficient conditions for the convergence of Mestimates in nonparametric regression settings notably extending existing results in the literature Our findings highlight the potential pitfalls of applying standard Mestimators in the presence of infinite variance and suggest modifications to enhance their robustness Through extensive simulations and realdata applications we demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed methods and their advantages over traditional estimators This work contributes to the growing body of knowledge on nonparametric regression techniques and provides valuable insights for practitioners dealing with complex data structures

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this paper we investigate the maximum likelihood estimation MLE of parameters in nearly nonstationary stable autoregressive AR processes a class of time series models that exhibits longrange dependence and heavytailed behavior Traditional methodologies often overlook the nuanced characteristics of nonstationarity inherent in stable distributions leading to potential biases in estimation We present a comprehensive framework for MLE that accommodates the unique features of nearly nonstationary stable AR processes including the formulation of the likelihood function and the derivation of asymptotic properties of the estimators Through simulation studies we demonstrate the robustness and efficacy of our proposed estimation approach compared to existing methods Furthermore we apply the framework to realworld financial datasets showcasing its practical relevance and effectiveness in capturing the underlying dynamics of nearly nonstationary series Our findings contribute to the statistical theory and practice of time series analysis providing a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners dealing with complex temporal data structures

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this paper we investigate the asymptotic properties of nearly nonstationary autoregressive processes of order one denoted as AR Our study focuses on the behavior of these processes when the autoregressive parameter is close to the unit root which leads to intricate challenges in statistical inference We derive the asymptotic distributions of key estimators including the ordinary least squares OLS estimator and the YuParker estimator under both stationary and nonstationary regimes Additionally we provide conditions that ensure the validity of statistical tests for parameter significance and model specification in nearly nonstationary settings We apply our results to establish confidence intervals and hypothesis tests illustrating their practical utility through simulations and a case study of economic time series data Our findings contribute to the theoretical understanding of nearly nonstationary processes while offering robust tools for applied researchers facing similar inference problems in empirical studies

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this paper we introduce a novel approach employing the Group Lasso method for analyzing time series data with structural breaks Traditional time series regression models often struggle to accurately capture the dynamics of series exhibiting abrupt changes in their underlying relationships The Group Lasso methodology designed for simultaneous variable selection and coefficient estimation offers a powerful framework for managing highdimensional data while accounting for these structural shifts We propose a systematic approach to identify and estimate the groups of variables that bear significant relationships with the dependent variable before and after a structural break Through extensive simulations and applications to realworld datasets we demonstrate that our Group Lasso model significantly outperforms conventional methods in terms of predictive accuracy and interpretability Our results highlight the models capability to not only detect structural breaks but also to effectively differentiate between relevant and irrelevant predictors in the presence of these breaks This research contributes to the growing body of literature on robust statistical techniques for time series analysis providing valuable insights for econometricians and data scientists dealing with complex temporal data

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: AbstractIn this study we present a comprehensive framework for the spatial modeling of regional variables aimed at enhancing our understanding of spatial patterns and their implications for regional analysis Leveraging advanced statistical techniques we explore the interplay between geographical factors and socioeconomic indicators employing both traditional regression models and contemporary geostatistical approaches Our methodology encompasses the application of spatial autocorrelation measures variogram analysis and kriging methods to incorporate spatial dependencies within regional datasets We illustrate our approach through a case study that examines the distribution of income levels across various regions revealing significant spatial heterogeneity and clustering effects The results underscore the importance of incorporating spatial considerations in statistical modeling highlighting nuances that conventional models may overlook By providing insights into the spatial dynamics of regional variables our research contributes to more informed decisionmaking in policy and planning contexts This work not only advances methodological practices in spatial statistics but also lays the groundwork for future investigations into the socioeconomic phenomena at play within and across regional boundaries

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: A robust local linear regression smoothing estimator for a nonparametric regression model with heavytailed dependent errors is considered in this paper Under certain regularity conditions the weak consistency and asymptotic distribution of the proposed estimators are obtained If the errors are shortrange dependent then the limiting distribution of the estimator is normal If the data are longrange dependent then the limiting distribution of the estimator is a stable distribution

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: A firstorder autoregressive process Y t Y t t Y is said to be nearly nonstationary when is close to one The limiting distribution of the leastsquares estimate b n b for is studied when Y t Y is nearly nonstationary By reparameterizing to be n being a fixed constant it is shown that the limiting distribution of n n t Y t b n converges to L L which is a quotient of stochastic integrals of standard Brownian motion This provides a reasonable alternative to the approximation of the distribution of n proposed by Ahtola and Tiao

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: ValueatRisk VaR is a commonly used risk measure adopted by financial engineers and regulators alike Many of the techniques used in calculating VaR however rely on simulations that can be difficult and time consuming One of the objectives of this paper is to conduct statistical inference for VaR based on saddle point approximation and volatility estimation Specifically by assuming that the loss distribution is a generalized hyperbolic we propose a quasiresidual based volatility estimate Because saddle point approximation furnishes a fast and accurate means to approximate the loss distribution and its percentiles including the VaR in particular it is then used to approximate the loss distribution of the quasiresiduals from which VaR can be estimated Simulation studies and data analysis confirm that the proposed methodology works well both in theory and practice

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: This paper studies the residual empirical process of long and shortmemory time series regression models and establishes its uniform expansion under a general framework The results are applied to the stochastic regression models and unstable autoregressive models For the longmemory noise it is shown that the limit distribution of the KolmogorovSmimov test statistic studied in Ho and Hsing Ann Statist does not hold when the stochastic regression model includes an unknown intercept or when the characteristic polynomial of the unstable autoregressive model has a unit root To this end two new statistics are proposed to test for the distribution of the longmemory noises of stochastic regression models and unstable autoregressive models

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: This paper studies the quasimaximum likelihood estimator QMLE of nonstationary GARCHp q models By expressing GARCH models in matrix form the loglikelihood function is written in terms of the product of random matrices Oseledecs multiplicative ergodic theorem is then used to establish the asymptotic properties of the loglikelihood function and thereby showing the weak consistency and the asymptotic normality of the QMLE for nonstationary GARCHp q models

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: This paper investigates the effectiveness of the Bartlett correction for empirical likelihood EL methods in the context of Gaussian longmemory time series Longmemory processes characterized by slowly decaying autocorrelations present unique challenges for statistical inference particularly regarding the estimation of confidence intervals and hypothesis testing The empirical likelihood approach offers a nonparametric alternative to traditional methods but its asymptotic properties can be compromised in the presence of longrange dependence We rigorously derive the asymptotic distribution of the empirical likelihood ratio under the Bartlett correction which adjusts for potential biases introduced by long memory Through extensive simulation studies we compare the corrected empirical likelihood method to conventional parametric approaches and naive empirical likelihood estimators highlighting its robustness and accuracy in capturing the true underlying distribution of the statistics Our findings contribute to the understanding of statistical inference in longmemory processes and provide a practical framework for researchers dealing with empirical likelihood in this domain The implications of our results extend to a broad spectrum of applied fields including economic time series analysis and environmental statistics where longmemory phenomena frequently arise

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: This paper investigates the convergence properties of stochastic integrals through the lens of white noise calculus establishing a robust framework for analyzing convergence in stochastic processes We begin by reviewing the foundational principles of white noise analysis and its implications for stochastic calculus highlighting how these tools can enhance our understanding of integrals driven by Gaussian white noise Utilizing rigorous mathematical techniques we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the convergence of stochastic integrals in various settings including both finite and infinitedimensional spaces Furthermore we explore the relationships between different modes of convergence almost sure in probability and in distribution providing illustrative examples that underscore the practical applications of our findings Our results contribute to the theoretical underpinnings of stochastic analysis and offer new insights applicable to fields such as finance physics and engineering where the modeling of uncertainty is paramount We conclude with a discussion of potential extensions of our work suggesting avenues for future research in the realm of nonlinear stochastic systems

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: The limiting distribution of the quantile estimate for the autoregressive coefficient of a nearintegrated first order autoregressive model with infinite variance errors is derived Since the limiting distribution depends on the unknown density function of the errors an empirical likelihood ratio statistic is proposed from which confidence intervals can be constructed for the near unit root model without knowing the density function Numerical simulations are conducted to compare the performance of the empirical likelihood method and the least squares procedure It is found that the empirical likelihood method outperforms the least squares procedure in general

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this study we propose a comprehensive framework for making statistical inferences in nonstationary Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity GARCH models specifically the GARCHp Q class Nonstationarity in financial data characterized by timevarying mean and volatility poses significant challenges for traditional GARCH modeling approaches which assume stationarity We derive asymptotic distributions for the estimators of model parameters under nonstationary conditions and introduce a robust estimation procedure that accommodates trends and structural breaks Our methodology includes a novel application of quasimaximum likelihood estimation in conjunction with unit root tests to validate the nonstationarity of the conditional variance We also explore the implications of nonstationarity on model diagnostics and forecasting performance Extensive Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate the finite sample properties of our estimators showcasing their consistency and asymptotic normality Finally we apply our developed framework to several financial time series datasets to illustrate its practical utility and effectiveness in capturing dynamic volatility patterns The results emphasize the importance of accounting for nonstationarity in GARCH models for accurate risk assessment and better decisionmaking in finance

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the Saddle Point Approximation SPA methodology as it applies to the estimation of ValueatRisk VaR under various market conditions VaR is a critical risk management tool in finance assessing the potential loss in value of an asset or portfolio over a specified time frame at a given confidence level Traditional methods of VaR estimation often rely on assumptions of normality or specific distributional forms which may not hold in realworld scenarios particularly in the presence of heavy tails and skewness By employing the SPA technique we derive more accurate approximations of the distribution of portfolio returns enabling a more robust estimation of VaR that accounts for the underlying volatility dynamics We compare the performance of the SPAbased VaR estimates against conventional approaches including historical simulation and parametric methods using both simulated data and historical market returns Our results demonstrate that the SPA method provides significant improvements in both accuracy and reliability particularly in periods of heightened market stress The implications for financial risk management and regulatory compliance are discussed emphasizing the need for adaptive approaches in the calculation of risk metrics This study contributes to the growing body of literature on advanced statistical techniques for risk assessment offering enhanced methodologies that can be integrated into risk management frameworks across financial institutions

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this paper a uniform over some parameter space moment bound for the inverse of Fishers information matrix is established This result is then applied to develop moment bounds for the normalized least squares estimate in nonlinear stochastic regression models The usefulness of these results is illustrated using time series models In particular an asymptotic expression for the mean squared prediction error of the least squares predictor in autoregressive moving average models is obtained This asymptotic expression provides a solid theoretical foundation for some model selection criteria

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In the realm of credit risk assessment understanding the dynamics of credit migration where borrowers transition between different credit risk categories is crucial for effective risk management and capital allocation This paper presents a comprehensive structural model of credit migration that integrates macroeconomic factors borrowerspecific characteristics and market conditions to predict changes in credit quality over time We employ a hybrid approach combining Markov chain processes and logistic regression to capture the probabilistic nature of migrations across credit ratings Our model is calibrated using a large dataset of historical credit ratings and associated economic indicators allowing us to identify key drivers of credit transitions We validate our model through outofsample testing demonstrating its superior predictive power compared to traditional models The findings provide a robust framework for financial institutions seeking to enhance their credit risk models facilitate stress testing and optimize portfolio management strategies Additionally we discuss the implications of credit migration dynamics on regulatory capital requirements and potential policy responses in changing economic landscapes

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: Credit migrations constitute the building blocks of modern risk management A firmspecific structural model of credit migration that incorporates the firms capital structure and the risk perception of rating agencies is proposed The proposed model employs the notion of distancetodefault which quantifies default probability The properties of Brownian excursions play an essential role in the analysis The proposed model not only allows the derivation of closedform credit transition probability but also provides plausible explanations for certain empirical evidence such as the default probability overlaps in ratings and the slowtorespond feature of rating agencies The proposed model is calibrated through simulations and applied to empirical data which show rating agencies risk perceptions to be significant The calibrated model allows calculation of the firmspecific transition probabilities of rated companies C Elsevier BV

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: Bartlett correction is one of the desirable features of empirical likelihood EL since it allows constructions of confidence regions with improved coverage probabilities Previous studies demonstrated the Bartlett correction of EL for independent observations and for shortmemory time series By establishing the validity of Edgeworth expansion for the signed root empirical loglikelihood ratio the validity of Bartlett correction of EL for Gaussian longmemory time series is established In particular orders of the coverage error of confidence regions can be reduced from log nn to log nn which is different from the classical rate of reduction from n to n

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: AbstractThis paper investigates the properties of residual empirical processes derived from both long and short memory time series models We delve into the theoretical underpinnings of residuals obtained from fitted linear models focusing on the implications of different memory structures on the asymptotic behavior of these residuals Building upon classical results in empirical process theory we establish convergence results for the residual empirical processes under various conditions pertaining to the underlying time series memory characteristics emphasizing the contrast between stationary short memory processes and nonstationary long memory processes We also provide practical applications of these findings in the context of model diagnostics and hypothesis testing illustrating how the behavior of residuals can inform the validation of model assumptions Our results contribute to the existing literature by bridging the gap between theory and practice in the analysis of time series data thereby enhancing the toolkit available for statisticians and econometricians dealing with complex temporal data structures Simulation studies are included to demonstrate the applicability of our theoretical results in realworld scenarios showcasing the robustness of residualbased approaches in both memory regimes

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the quantile inference for nearintegrated autoregressive time series characterized by infinite variance We build upon the framework of traditional autoregressive models extending our analysis to accommodate the unique attributes of nearintegrated processes which exhibit long memory and trending behavior By employing advanced statistical techniques and asymptotic theory we derive robust quantile estimation methods that effectively address the challenges posed by infinite variance Our results demonstrate the consistency and asymptotic normality of the proposed quantile estimators along with the validity of inferential procedures in the presence of persistent shocks and unpredictable fluctuations We also provide simulation studies that illustrate the practical application of our methods and their superior performance compared to existing approaches in the literature Finally we highlight the implications of our findings for econometric modeling and forecasting in fields such as finance and environmental studies where nearintegrated processes with infinite variance are prevalent

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this paper we examine the uniform moment bounds of Fishers information in the context of time series models Fishers information is a fundamental quantity in statistics that quantifies the amount of information that an observable random variable carries about an unknown parameter We establish new uniform moment bounds for Fishers information providing rigorous frameworks for understanding its behavior across various parameter spaces and distributions Our analysis leverages techniques from functional analysis and probability theory to derive bounds that are uniformly applicable over a class of time series models Applications of these results are demonstrated in the context of maximum likelihood estimation and hypothesis testing highlighting how uniform moment bounds can enhance the robustness of parameter estimation in nonstationary and dependent structures commonly encountered in time series data We illustrate our findings through simulations and empirical examples suggesting that our bounds could serve as valuable tools for statisticians and data scientists working with dynamic models This work not only contributes to the theoretical understanding of Fishers information but also provides practical implications for its utilization in analyzing timedependent phenomena

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: Random walk models driven by GARCH errors are widely applicable in diverse areas in finance and econometrics For a firstorder autoregressive model driven by GARCH errors let phi over cap n be the least squares estimate of the autoregressive coefficient The asymptotic distribution of phi over cap n is given in Ling and Li when the GARCH errors have finite variances In this paper the limit distribution of phi over cap n is established as functionals of a stable process when the GARCH errors are heavytailed with infinite variances An estimate of the tail index of the limiting stable process is proposed and its asymptotic properties are derived Furthermore it is shown that the least absolute deviations procedure works well under the unitroot and heavytailed GARCH setting This research provides a relatively broad treatment of unitroot GARCH models that includes the commonly entertained unitroot IGARCH scenario

text: In this study we propose a comprehensive framework for making statistical inferences in nonstationary Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity GARCH models specifically the GARCHp Q class Nonstationarity in financial data characterized by timevarying mean and volatility poses significant challenges for traditional GARCH modeling approaches which assume stationarity We derive asymptotic distributions for the estimators of model parameters under nonstationary conditions and introduce a robust estimation procedure that accommodates trends and structural breaks Our methodology includes a novel application of quasimaximum likelihood estimation in conjunction with unit root tests to validate the nonstationarity of the conditional variance We also explore the implications of nonstationarity on model diagnostics and forecasting performance Extensive Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate the finite sample properties of our estimators showcasing their consistency and asymptotic normality Finally we apply our developed framework to several financial time series datasets to illustrate its practical utility and effectiveness in capturing dynamic volatility patterns The results emphasize the importance of accounting for nonstationarity in GARCH models for accurate risk assessment and better decisionmaking in finance

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this paper we investigate the properties and implications of nonstationary autoregressive processes with infinite variance expanding upon traditional models that assume finite variance We introduce a novel framework that captures the dynamics of nonstationary time series while acknowledging the complexities introduced by infinite variance Using a blend of theoretical derivations and empirical analysis we demonstrate how these processes can be characterized by their asymptotic behavior and longrange dependence properties We establish sufficient conditions for the existence of such processes and provide influential examples to illustrate their applications in fields such as finance and environmental science The consequences of modeling choices are examined revealing that failure to account for infinite variance can lead to significant underestimation of risks and misinterpretation of longterm forecasts Our findings suggest new methodologies for analyzing and forecasting nonstationary time series data paving the way for enhanced models that incorporate the intricacies of infinite variance dynamics Through simulation studies we evaluate the performance of our proposed estimators emphasizing their robustness in capturing the unpredictable nature of realworld phenomena Overall our work contributes to the existing literature by providing a comprehensive analysis of nonstationary autoregressive processes in the context of infinite variance offering critical insights for researchers and practitioners

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this paper we investigate the characteristics and implications of nearly nonstationary seasonal timeseries data which exhibit both persistent seasonal patterns and gradual shifts in their mean and variance We begin by formalizing the concept of nearly nonstationarity distinguishing it from traditional stationary and nonstationary timeseries paradigms Using both empirical analysis and simulation studies we demonstrate that standard seasonal decomposition methods can yield misleading results when applied to nearly nonstationary series often failing to adequately capture underlying trends and seasonality To address this issue we propose a novel framework that integrates techniques from seasonal adjustment trend extraction and nonstationary timeseries analysis Our methodology employs a combination of wavelet transforms and adaptive filtering to effectively isolate seasonal components while accounting for timevarying structures We apply our approach to several realworld datasets including economic indicators and climaterelated variables illustrating its effectiveness in improving forecast accuracy and interpretability Through rigorous statistical testing and validation we provide insights into the stability and dynamics of nearly nonstationary seasonal timeseries emphasizing the importance of recognizing underlying data complexities in practical applications This work contributes to the growing field of timeseries analysis by offering innovative tools and methodologies tailored for the unique challenges posed by nearly nonstationary seasonal processes paving the way for more robust statistical practices in datadriven decisionmaking

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this paper we investigate the asymptotic properties of unstable autoregressive timeseries models with drifts Traditional approaches for timeseries analysis often assume stationarity which may not hold in the presence of instability and nonconstant dynamics We propose a comprehensive framework for deriving asymptotic inference for such models focusing on key statistical properties including consistency asymptotic normality and the behavior of estimators as the sample size tends to infinity By employing advanced techniques from the theory of stochastic processes we establish the conditions under which asymptotic results can be achieved despite the presence of drifts that exacerbate instability Our findings are supported by simulations and realdata applications demonstrating the practical relevance of our theoretical contributions This work provides foundational insights for analysts dealing with complex timeseries data in various fields paving the way for improved modeling and inference strategies in unstable timeseries environments

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this paper we investigate parameter inference in nearly nonstationary time series a common phenomenon in empirical data where the underlying processes exhibit longterm trends or shifts that can complicate traditional statistical modeling We introduce a novel framework that integrates methodologies from both time series analysis and nonstationary process theory enabling robust estimation of parameters in the presence of subtle nonstationary behaviors Our approach employs a combination of statespace models and filtering techniques to disentangle the stationary and nonstationary components facilitating a clearer understanding of the underlying dynamics We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through a series of simulation studies and realworld applications highlighting its superior performance in parameter estimation accuracy when compared to conventional techniques Furthermore we discuss the implications of our findings for practitioners dealing with economic environmental and social data that display nearly nonstationary characteristics Our results contribute to the ongoing discourse on improving statistical inference in complex time series providing a comprehensive toolset for researchers and analysts in various fields

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In this paper we introduce a novel approach employing the Group Lasso method for analyzing time series data with structural breaks Traditional time series regression models often struggle to accurately capture the dynamics of series exhibiting abrupt changes in their underlying relationships The Group Lasso methodology designed for simultaneous variable selection and coefficient estimation offers a powerful framework for managing highdimensional data while accounting for these structural shifts We propose a systematic approach to identify and estimate the groups of variables that bear significant relationships with the dependent variable before and after a structural break Through extensive simulations and applications to realworld datasets we demonstrate that our Group Lasso model significantly outperforms conventional methods in terms of predictive accuracy and interpretability Our results highlight the models capability to not only detect structural breaks but also to effectively differentiate between relevant and irrelevant predictors in the presence of these breaks This research contributes to the growing body of literature on robust statistical techniques for time series analysis providing valuable insights for econometricians and data scientists dealing with complex temporal data

text: Consider an ARp process where t is a sequence of iid random variables lying in the domain of attraction of a stable law with index a This time series is said to be a nonstationary ARp process if at least one of its characteristic roots lies on the unit circle The limit distribution of the least squares estimator LSE of for with infinite variance innovation t is established in this paper In particular by virtue of the result of Kurtz and Protter of stochastic integrals it is shown that the limit distribution of the LSE is a functional of integrated stable process Simulations for the estimator of beta and its limit distribution are also given

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: An autoregressive time series is said to be unstable if all of its characteristics roots lie on or outside the unit circle This paper aims at developing the asymptotic inference for the least squares estimates of unstable autoregressive time series with drifts Our framework allows for both constant and periodic drifts The presence of a nonzero drift in the series affects the asymptotic behavior in a surprising and interesting way For models with constant nonzero drifts conventional asymptotic normal theory is attained only for unit root time series but not in general For models with periodic drifts degenerate nonnormal asymptotics are resulted for unit root series However for models with roots lying on the unit circle which are not equal to unity nonnormal asymptotics are always attained for both constant and periodic drifts unless there are confounding effects between the periodicities of the drifts and the locations of the roots Our approach is based on a componentwise argument used in Chan and Wei The theories developed here extend much earlier work and help to clarify the intrinsic critical phenomena in the field of unstable time series

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: A time series is said to be nearly nonstationary if some of its characteristic roots are close to the unit circle For a seasonal time series such a notion of near nonstationarity is studied in a double array setting This approach not only furnishes a natural transition between stationarity and nonstationarity but also unifies the corresponding asymptotic theories in a seasonal time series context The general theory is expressed in terms of functionals of independent diffusion processes The asymptotic results have applications to estimation and testing in a nearly nonstationary situation and serve as a useful alternative to the common practice of seasonal adjustment

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: A firstorder autoregressive AR time series Yt Yt t is said to be nearly nonstationary if is close to For a nearly nonstationary AR model it is shown that the limiting distribution of the least squares estimate of obtained by Chan and Wei can be expressed as a functional of the OrnsteinUhlenbeck process This alternative expression provides a simple and efficient means to tabulate the percentiles of the limiting distribution that furnishes a useful procedure to test for near nonstationarity Based on the eigenvalueeigenfunction consideration it is shown that the OrnsteinUhlenbeck formulation possesses an infinite series expansion that extends the result of Dickey and Fuller to the nearly nonstationary model Numerical calculations based on different representations of the limiting distribution are performed and compared It is found that the OrnsteinUhlenbeck expression provides a better algorithm for tabulating the percentiles Applications to other time series are also considered

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: This paper investigates the inferential properties of unitroot models disturbed by errors characterized by infinite variance GARCH Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity processes Traditional approaches to unitroot testing often assume that the error terms have finite variance potentially leading to misleading conclusions when applied to time series data exhibiting heavytailed distributions By extending the classical unitroot frameworks to accommodate the infinite variance case we develop new testing procedures that maintain consistency and asymptotic normality even under these conditions Our analysis includes both theoretical derivations and empirical evaluations demonstrating that conventional tests can yield invalid results in the presence of GARCH errors with infinite variance We propose a robust framework for conducting inference utilizing generalized methods of moments GMM to estimate parameters and perform hypothesis testing Through Monte Carlo simulations we assess the size and power of our proposed tests compared to existing methodologies Finally we apply our findings to realworld financial time series data illustrating the practical implications of ignoring the potential for infinite variance in GARCH models The results highlight the importance of careful selection of testing procedures when analyzing unitroot processes in volatile environments

author: Ngai Hang Chan
text: In the analysis of nonstationary time series traditional empirical processes often fall short in capturing the complexities introduced by timevarying distributions and trends This paper introduces a novel framework of marked empirical processes tailored specifically for nonstationary time series data By incorporating markers that reflect significant features of the time series such as trends seasonality and structural breaks our approach enhances the interpretability and robustness of empirical distributions over various temporal intervals We establish consistency and asymptotic properties of the proposed marked empirical processes and demonstrate their efficacy through simulations and realworld applications Our findings suggest that marked empirical processes provide an effective tool for modeling nonstationary phenomena offering improved insights into the underlying dynamics of complex temporal data This work contributes to the broader field of statistical methods for time series analysis by extending the utility of empirical processes in nonstationary contexts thereby facilitating better inference in diverse applications ranging from finance to environmental science
